posts.title: Open quay Saturday: 6 February 2027
posts.excerpt: On Saturday 6 February 2027 the quay at Pier 3 is open from 10:00 to 13:00 for visitors who want to see the harbour the cadets train on.
posts.content:
Hatoba College opens the quay at Pier 3 on Saturday 6 February 2027, from 10:00 to 13:00. That Saturday is the first Saturday of the month, which is the college's standing open day. The address is Pier 3, 4 Quay Road, Port Ellery. You do not need a ticket price from this notice, because the college has not published one. Come to the quay itself, not to a town-centre office. There is no second address.

The open quay is how a visitor sees the harbour that the course treats as a classroom. Bollards, coiled ropes and the small training vessel are out on the pier. Cadets who are already in the intake will be about, and so will visitors. It is a working quay in daylight, not a staged tour with a script. If the mist is low, you will still find the office door by staying on Pier 3 and asking there.

The January intake began on 12 January 2027. By 6 February those cadets are in the early weeks of Harbour Foundation, the part of the course called shore school, which runs through week 4. Week 4 is when a cadet plots a first bearing on a paper chart. You may see charts and the quay on the same morning. You will not be put into the class, and a conversation on the pier is not the week-4 exercise. Muster at 07:30, the simulator debrief at 12:00 and line-handling at 16:00 are weekday anchors of the course. They are not the timetable of this Saturday. The Saturday window is 10:00 to 13:00 only.

People often arrive with an application in mind. The open quay can help you decide whether to enquire. It does not take the place of the four steps. Those steps remain an enquiry, a medical and an eyesight test, an interview at Pier 3, and then a place confirmed in writing. Applicants are 18 or over. The EUR 90 application and berth assessment is a deposit counted inside the programme fee, and it is not collected as an entrance charge at the gangway on Saturday.

Because 12 January has passed, a visitor on 6 February is not joining that intake by walking the quay. Harbour Foundation places are 18 cadets on an intake, and that January group is already in shore school. The later intake months are April and September. The college has published three further dates for the January group, and they are worth knowing so you do not confuse them with a start date for yourself. Assessment for the January intake is 26 March 2027. A berth, if one has been arranged, is confirmed in writing on 2 April 2027, the Friday of week 12, after the assessment. Those dates do not move to the Saturday you visit.

The office is ordinarily open Monday to Friday, 08:30 to 17:00, and the college is closed on Sundays and public holidays. This open Saturday is the exception that the calendar already names. If you want a formal interview, book it for a weekday in those office hours. Phone +00 0000 0000, or email admissions@hatoba-college.example. On the form, choose January, April or September as the intake of interest, and write the programme in the message. Harbour Foundation is 12 weeks. The other programmes have their own lengths and fees on the programmes page.

Nothing you are shown on 6 February is an offer of a berth. The college arranges training berths with unnamed operators of three kinds: coastal ferry, harbour tug, and short-sea cargo. Confirmation is a letter after assessment, not a conversation beside a bollard. The cadet stories on the site are about named people from earlier training. They are useful, and they are not a forecast for the 18 cadets who started in January, nor for whoever starts in April or September.

If you cannot come on 6 February, the open quay returns on the first Saturday of the following month, again from 10:00 to 13:00. The college's monthly email lists those Saturdays and the intake dates. One email a month is the whole of that list. To ask for it, use the newsletter form. The form opens your email app, and you are not subscribed until you send the message to admissions@hatoba-college.example. Bring a plain question on 6 February if you do come: which programme, which month, and whether you still need a medical and an eyesight test before an interview. Those are the facts the quay can help you line up.

posts.title: What the week-12 assessment looks like
posts.excerpt: The assessment closes the twelve weeks; the berth is confirmed in writing on the Friday.
posts.content: Week 12 is the assessment. A cadet plots a bearing, keeps a short watch on the simulator and answers questions from an instructor. The training berth is confirmed in writing on the Friday of that week.

posts.title: A day on the simulator bridge
posts.excerpt: Weeks 5 to 7 move the cadets onto the full-mission bridge simulator.
posts.content: In weeks 5 to 7 the cadets stand watches on the full-mission bridge simulator. Each watch ends with a debrief at the radar, where the cadet explains the bearing, the traffic and the choice just made.
